Author: Kyuuso
Name: Anima Helper
Punchline: Heavensward Anima relic: buys, farms and turns in for you.
Description: Early beta. Takes your Anima (Heavensward) weapons through their stages: accepts the stage quests, buys the Poetics items (farming Poetics with AutoDuty when short), runs the step duties through AutoDuty and turns the quests in. Needs AutoDuty for the farms and vnavmesh for walking to the NPCs.
TestingChangelog:
0.7.23, changes since 0.5.15:
- Gerolt's turn-in still stopped at the second Request window in 0.7.22: it opens about 50 ms after the first one closes, and the plugin only looked for a window that had closed. A Request window still open 1 s after Hand Over with no item in it now counts as the next one.
- Coming into Its Own turn-in: Gerolt asks in two Request windows, the weapon first and then the four materials. The plugin handed over the weapon and stood still at the second window with Hand Over greyed out. A new Request window that opens after the first closes is now filled and handed over too, up to 4 windows per step.
- Seal purchase for the Maelstrom stopped with "Could not get to Storm Quartermaster: no aetheryte known for that zone". He stands in Limsa Lominsa Upper Decks, which has no aetheryte of its own. Trips to such a zone now teleport to the city aetheryte and take the aethernet shard in that zone through Lifestream (The Aftcastle here), up to 3 tries.
- Coming into Its Own: after the Cristiana trade for Enchanted Rubber took the 10 Unidentifiable Bone, Start saw 0 bones held and farmed Poetics to buy them again. A Poetics item now counts as bought once a trade that uses it is done, for each item on its own; before, the buying only ended once all four trades were done.
- Poetics items: Auriana in Mor Dhona sells the unidentifiable items from the same "Allagan Tomestones of Poetics (Special Arms)" shop as Hismena. Without ADS, a player in Mor Dhona now buys from Auriana instead of teleporting to Idyllshire. ADS already picked the nearer of the two. Shopping lists both vendors.
- Poetics farm: The Aetherochemical Research Facility ran unsynced with an unrestricted party, where "enemies will not yield EXP or items" and no Poetics came. It now runs through Duty Support (AutoDuty or DAD), as ZodiacHelper does, whenever the Poetics duty has Duty Support; other duties stay unsynced Regular.
- A choice inside a cutscene (CutSceneSelectString, "What did you hear?" after Toughening Up) was left open and the run stood still. It now picks the first answer, as with the other flavour questions, and Escape is not sent while it is open.
- Turn-in: the game refuses it with the previous weapon in hand ("You cannot complete this quest until the following conditions are met: Must possess the necessary item.", Toughening Up), and the run picked the quest every 4 s. Before a turn-in the plugin now equips another weapon of the same kind from the armoury; with none there it stops and says so.
- Cutscenes in NPC talks are skipped by the plugin: Escape while one plays, then Yes to "Skip cutscene?". Ardashir's talk in the South Shroud waited for the player to press Escape.
- NPC talks: a quest talk that plays a cutscene asks "Skip cutscene?" (Yes. / No.), and the run read it as the NPC's menu and stopped ("Ardashir's menu has none of [Toughening Up]", South Shroud). It now answers Yes.
- Duty unlocks check what the unlock quest needs first, as ZodiacHelper does: duties a quest asks for cleared (Quest.InstanceContent) are run before it. "Not Easy Being Green" was not offered ("Dungeon Requirement: The Wanderer's Palace"); now The Wanderer's Palace is cleared first through AutoDuty or DAD, and a locked one gets its own unlock quest before that. Among the quests that have a duty as a step, the ones that open content come first.
- Revenant's Toll: arriving there on the mount failed the trip at once with "could not land next to ... in 60 s" (the dismount there never started its clock). It now gets off the mount and walks on.
- WigglyQuest paths for the duty unlock quests its public set lacks: It's Definitely Pirates, The Wrath of Qarn, For Keep's Sake, Not Easy Being Green (Toughening Up), One More Night in Amdapor, The Fires of Sohm Al, Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Retells Your Story (Born Again Anima). Installed only when WigglyQuest has no path of its own.
- Duty unlocks: the plugin accepts the unlock quest itself before WigglyQuest gets it. WigglyQuest flew into the wall by the quest giver of "It's Definitely Pirates" in Revenant's Toll and kept hovering there; the plugin's own trip walks in that town. A quest that has the duty as a step opens it on accept, so WigglyQuest is then not needed.
- Locked duties are unlocked first, before the stage starts, as ZodiacHelper does before A Relic Reborn: every duty the stage still runs (and the Poetics duty when the Poetics held do not pay for the items left) is checked, and a locked one gets its quest done through WigglyQuest. Steps lists them as "Unlock ..." with a Run button, and the Stages tab marks a locked duty. Before, a locked dungeon stopped the run halfway through Toughening Up.
- Duty unlocks: a locked duty that no quest names as its unlock (Quest.InstanceContentUnlock) stopped the run with "no quest unlocks it". The ten Toughening Up dungeons are all like that. The plugin now also looks for one-time quests that have the duty as a step ("It's Definitely Pirates" for Sastasha (Hard)), takes the one with the fewest quests still to do, and runs it through WigglyQuest. WigglyQuest is stopped as soon as the duty opens, so it does not walk into the duty itself.
- NPC trades (Syndony's nodules, Cristiana's goods): the exchange row opens the item Request window with the cost items, and the trade stopped there with "the NPC asks for items this step does not hand in". It now fills the window and presses Trade.
- Shop windows: the row of an item counted every window text that is also an item name, and the job filter list has some ("Sage"). At Syndony the Astral Nodule came out as row 2 of a 2-row shop, and the exchange dialog opened on that row crashed the game. The row is now the item's place in the shop's own list. The exchange dialog that opens after the click gets its Exchange button pressed, and the list is not clicked again while it is open.
- Shop windows: item names carry colour and link codes, so a shop lookup by name never matched ("Astral Nodule is not in this shop" at Syndony). Window texts are now read without those codes.
- No vnavmesh path is asked for while the zone's mesh is not ready (a zone vnavmesh has not built yet). Paths asked for during the build failed, the stops after them cancelled the build, and it started over: the Anima FATE farm skipped three FATEs in the Sea of Clouds that way.
- FATE farm: in a zone vnavmesh had not built yet (Sea of Clouds), the farm asked for paths while the mesh was being built. They failed, the build was cancelled and started over, and three FATEs were skipped as out of reach. The farm now waits until the mesh is ready and shows the build progress.
- Revenant's Toll is walked on foot: no mount for an NPC there, and a player who arrives flying gets off first. Flying to Syndony ended against a wall, and a ground path started in the air never found its way.
- Trips to an NPC whose spot is under a roof (Rowena in Revenant's Toll) flew at it until 5 stuck checks failed the trip: vnavmesh never found a flight path there. After two stuck checks the trip now goes on the ground.
- Main tab: it said "1 part(s) by hand" for the luminous crystals that Start now farms. It names each part still left to you instead, and leaves out the FATE farm and the seal purchase when Settings has them on.
- New Manual > Shopping: what the ticked jobs still need from their next stage to Lux (Poetics items, Cristiana's goods, luminous crystals, Crystal Sand), with what you hold, the Poetics still to spend on items and the seals the goods cost. Buy spends the Poetics or seals you hold on an item, up to what is needed, so neither sits at its cap. Teleport goes to the nearest aetheryte.
- Start switches to the job's first gearset when a quest or duty needs that job, and equips the previous Anima weapon when Ardashir or a duty asks for it in hand. It used to stop with "Switch to ..." or "Equip ...". A job with no gearset still stops and says so.
- Soul without Life: a FATE farm gets the six luminous crystals (Sea of Clouds, Azys Lla, Churning Mists, Coerthas Western Highlands, Dravanian Forelands, and the Dravanian Hinterlands through the Prologue Gate shard in Idyllshire), then Syndony trades them for the Astral and Umbral Nodules ("Offer luminous crystals."). Only the crystals a trade still needs are farmed. Settings: "Farm the luminous crystals in FATEs" (on) and "Skip FATEs longer than 15 minutes". It needs vnavmesh and a combat plugin.
- Coming into Its Own: the talk to Cristiana at the quest's first step was missing, so Start went straight to the turn-in. It now talks to her, then trades the unidentifiable items and goods in her "Anima Weapon Materials" shop.
- Settings: "Buy Cristiana's goods with Grand Company seals" (off by default). It buys the 16 goods from your company's quartermaster, 5,000 seals each (80,000 for all), at the rank of Second Lieutenant.
- Future Proof: Blamprest's second talk hands over the 50 Singing Clusters. The quest is accepted with the previous weapon equipped, as its text asks.
- Body and Soul and Words of Wisdom: the Rowena step in Idyllshire is done by the plugin. It used to stop there.
- Steps lists what a part by hand still lacks, and the FATE farm and the seal purchase have Run buttons.
- Still by hand: Ulan's Crystal Sand and the refining in A Dream Fulfilled.
- Manual > Steps replaces Next step. It lists every step of a job's current stage in the order the quest asks for them: the quest it needs, the accept, each Poetics item, talks, side quest, each duty, the parts by hand and the turn-in. Done steps are greyed out, the first one left says "next", and each step has its own Run button that does only that step. A job picker shows any job, not only the one Start works on next.
- Duties in Steps have a tick box instead of the - and + buttons. A duty run out of order does not move the count; tick it if it counted.
- Start bought the Poetics items a second time once they were spent: after the Cristiana trade (6,000 Poetics at Coming into Its Own), Ulan's refining, the Blamprest trade or Some Assembly Required. Ticking that part, or finishing the side quest, now ends the buying for the stage.
- The remarks on Toughening Up (dungeon order) and Best Friends Forever (quests it needs) stopped Start until they were ticked. They are notes now and do not stop it.
- The Main tab duty count includes the duties the quest journal has already moved past.
- New tabs. Main has Start, the jobs, what the next stage needs and any missing plugin. Manual has Next step (runs one step and stops), Poetics (farms the Poetics duty to the cap, nothing else) and Stages (every stage with its items, duties and parts by hand). Status and Settings stay.
- Settings > Plugins lists every plugin this one works with, whether it is loaded, and a button that copies its repository link.
- Settings > Combat plugin (Auto, Rotation Solver, BossMod, Wrath Combo) is set in AutoDuty for each run. During DAD or AutoDuty runs started here, the picked plugin is turned back on after 3 s in combat when it went off; Wrath goes through its lease, BossMod gets a preset that has the job's rotation.
- Settings > Dungeon coffers: the runner's own settings (default), boss coffers only, every coffer, or none.
- Gear repair between duty runs once a piece is at or below 30 % (Settings > Gear repair): Dark Matter first, then Alistair in Limsa Lominsa Lower Decks for what is left.
- Duty cutscenes are skipped during runs (Escape only while a cutscene plays).
- Trips to an NPC wait up to 3 minutes to leave a duty before teleporting. The teleport tries used to run out while AutoDuty was still inside.
- When the game refuses the dismount next to an NPC (roof, slope, water), the plugin tries other ground nearby for up to 60 s. It used to give up after 5 dismounts.
- Duty unlocks: when WigglyQuest hovers on the mount at an NPC for 8 s, the plugin lands and starts the quest again.
- A draw error in the mini window is written to the log instead of replacing the window.
Not tested in game yet: all of the above.

Description:
# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

Author: Akari
Name: Mahjong Advisor
Punchline: Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.
Description: Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.
Changelog: v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.
